bull.t: Strong commercial growth and franchise adoption
bull.b: Rapid AMVUTTRA uptake, expanding prescriber adoption and strong TTR growth demonstrate meaningful product-market fit. The scale of recurring product revenue and continued first-line patient growth support a durable commercial platform.

The shift from prior losses to substantial earnings and cash generation improves funding capacity for clinical development and commercialization. Free cash flow equal to roughly 90% of net income also supports the quality of reported profitability.

Multiple clinical programs and geographic partnerships diversify future growth beyond current products. Expansion into new indications, regions and data-driven discovery can extend the RNAi platform's commercial runway over the medium term.

bear.b: The guidance reduction shows that launch-period demand may have benefited from temporary pent-up switching. Although growth remains strong, normalization creates a higher execution burden and raises uncertainty around the pace of future franchise expansion.

bear.t: Margin pressure and rising operating investment
bear.b: Higher royalties are reducing product economics while Phase III development and launch spending are increasing. Sustained cost growth could limit operating leverage and make future profitability more dependent on continued high revenue growth.

bear.t: Meaningful leverage and earnings durability risk
bear.b: The balance sheet has improved alongside the turnaround, but leverage remains material and the recent earnings record is short. A normalization in product growth or renewed cost pressure could weaken coverage and reduce financial flexibility.
